html:
A city at the southern edge of the Air Mountains in Niger, seat of a Tuareg sultanate from about the 1440s and a main stop on the caravan routes between the Hausa lands and North Africa.

The Songhai Empire took it about 1500, and its mud-brick minaret, first raised in 1515, is the tallest such structure in the world. Salt, slaves, cloth and goods crossed through it on the trans-Saharan trade, and the Tuareg of the Air controlled the routes. Its old centre became a World Heritage Site in 2013. In recent decades Agadez has been the main gathering point for migrants heading across the desert to Libya and Europe. See also the Kaocen revolt.
sum: A city at the southern edge of the Air Mountains in Niger, seat of a Tuareg sultanate from about the 1440s and a main stop on the caravan routes between the Hausa lands and North Africa.
